Ugmuls 5.5e Automation · Detailed Summary

Class features.
Built into the roll.

Give players their class choices when they need them, and let the module handle the follow-through.

Automations → Unique Classes

Your class abilities,
right when you need them.

Choose your smite, unleash a maneuver, or add your class’s extra damage as you make the attack. Relevant options appear in the roll, with a preview of the damage you’re about to deal. The module tracks supported resources and once-per-turn uses, helping players focus on their next move and giving the GM less to keep track of. Explore the class sections below to see what’s supported.

Artificer

  • Flash of Genius: When an ally just misses a check or saving throw, the Artificer can help directly from the roll’s chat card. One click adds their Intelligence bonus and spends the feature use and Reaction—no separate roll or mental arithmetic.
  • Spell-Storing Item: Let the Artificer equip the party with spells. During a Long Rest, or by using the feature, the player chooses their own character or a friendly character on the map, selects a weapon or spellcasting focus from that character’s inventory, and chooses the spell to store. The module adds the stored spell to that item, ready for its holder to use. That character can cast it straight from the item, making attacks, prompting saves and rolling damage or healing as the spell requires. Charges are tracked separately from the holder’s spell slots, the spell uses the Artificer’s casting strength, and the holder manages concentration when needed. The GM does not have to copy spells or edit another player’s inventory by hand.
  • Alchemist: Brew and hand out Experimental Elixirs in one table after a Long Rest. Roll each bottle, choose its effect on a 6, and send it straight to a party member’s inventory. Unused bottles from the previous rest clear automatically. Alchemical Savant adds its bonus where the player rolls healing or eligible spell damage, and Alchemical Eruption offers its extra burst after qualifying damage is dealt.
  • Armorer: Suit up and attack with the armor’s weapons using the right Intelligence and enhancement bonuses. Guardian Thunder Pulse marks the creature you hit, discouraging it from attacking your allies, then clears the effect when its duration ends.
  • Battle Smith: Add Arcane Jolt while rolling damage from a qualifying magic weapon or Steel Defender attack. When a nearby enemy attacks an ally, the Defender’s owner can click Deflect Attack on that attack’s card. The result updates for Disadvantage, including a new miss, and Improved Deflection offers its return damage when available.
  • Artillerist: Casting through an Arcane Firearm? Add its extra damage while rolling the spell, with the bonus kept to one use per casting. Keep using Foundry’s familiar summon and command controls for your cannons.
  • Cartographer: Faerie Fire becomes a team tool: outlined enemies offer attack Advantage, and the Cartographer’s qualifying damage includes the Guided Precision choice. The module tracks its turn limit and avoids unnecessary concentration prompts for the protected spell.
  • Reanimator: Choose your companion’s modifications as you summon it, rather than editing its sheet afterward. Improved Reanimation upgrades Death Burst for you. When it is time for Life Transfer, confirm the sacrifice: the companion’s remaining HP heals the caster, its burst is centered on its position, and a summary shows the health moved. Life Jolt and other unsupported modification triggers remain manual.
  • Companion turns: Steel Defenders and other supported companions that act with their owner can stay off the initiative list. Their turn effects and recoverable abilities follow the owner’s turn, while each companion keeps its own Reaction and resources.

0.8.3 feature details →

Barbarian

CoreBerserkerWild HeartWorld Tree

Barbarians live to attack. With so many features triggered by an attack or damage roll, going back to add dice or adjust results can get confusing. Now those choices are built right into your Attack and Damage rolls—choose your strike, add your damage, and keep the fight moving.

  • Reckless Attack Choose Reckless right in the attack window. Its benefits and the enemy’s Advantage against you are tracked until your next turn, so you do not need to add and remove the effect yourself.
  • Frenzy Rage, attack recklessly, and roll your first qualifying hit: Frenzy’s extra damage joins the weapon damage automatically, including critical hits.
  • Zealot · Divine Fury While raging, add Divine Fury to your first qualifying hit each turn. Pick Radiant or Necrotic alongside the damage roll; the module adds the right bonus and tracks the use.
  • Zealot · Fanatical Focus A failed save offers a second chance right on its card. Click to reroll with the Rage bonus; the replacement result is used and the once-per-Rage use is tracked.
  • Zealot · Zealous Presence Inspire your allies and let the effect handle their attack and save Advantage until your next turn. It stays active across multiple rolls without being consumed by the first attack.
  • Brutal Strike Choose Brutal in the attack window to trade Reckless Advantage for a harder, more disruptive hit. The module tracks the turn’s chosen Brutal attack, including when it misses.
  • Brutal effects in damage Configuration On a hit, choose the blow’s effect alongside its damage: push, slow, stagger or sunder as your level allows. The extra damage rolls with the weapon, and supported conditions apply and expire for you. Move pushed tokens at the table.
  • Sundered The next eligible ally’s attack gets the +5 bonus, then consumes the opening whether it hits or misses. Canceling an attack does not waste it.
  • Staggered The target’s next save receives Disadvantage, while its restriction on Opportunity Attacks remains for the rest of the effect’s duration.

Rage, Strength and staying on your feet

  • Indomitable Might. Roll a Strength check or save as usual. If the total is below the Barbarian’s Strength score, the module raises it and labels the result.
  • Linked Rage benefits. Start Rage and supported benefits such as Primal Knowledge come with it. If Relentless Rage can keep you standing at 0 HP, its save is offered and the increasing difficulty is tracked.
  • Reckless cleanup. Use Reckless every round without filling the sheet with old copies of the same effect.

Berserker

  • Mindless Rage. Starting Rage clears Charmed and Frightened and supplies the feature’s protection while Rage lasts.
  • Intimidating Presence. Frighten nearby enemies, with repeat saves and condition cleanup following the affected creatures. Frenzy’s damage remains part of the normal attack flow.

Wild Heart

  • Choose before Rage. Pick your Wild Heart animal benefits in one window as you start Rage, including the later Power of the Wilds choice. Cancel if you are not ready; no use is spent.
  • Benefits follow the choice. Your selected animal applies its supported defenses, flight or ally/enemy aura benefits. These stay connected to Rage, so you spend less time swapping effects. Situational movement choices remain yours.
  • Ram and Aspects. Use the Ram follow-up after a qualifying hit to knock the target Prone. Choose Owl, Panther or Salmon from the Aspect card to replace the previous benefit; daily switching limits remain table-managed.

World Tree

  • Vitality Surge. Start Rage and receive your Barbarian-level temporary HP immediately, keeping a higher amount if you already have one. Extending the same Rage does not refill it.
  • Life-Giving Force. Use the feature’s healing action when you need it. Other World Tree choices and decisions about ending temporary HP stay in the players’ hands.

Bard

Bards live to inspire. They live to taunt. Adding your dice to an existing roll no longer means working it out afterward. Prompts appear directly on eligible rolls, only when you have the resources to spend, and automatically use the right die size.

  • Bardic Inspiration Give Inspiration, then let the recipient use it from a failed attack, save or check card. The right Bardic die is added to the existing result and the grant is spent—no rerolling the d20.
  • Lore · Cutting Words An eligible enemy hit or damage roll offers Cutting Words when the Bard can react. Roll the Bardic die from that card to lower the result before damage is applied.
  • Lore · Peerless Skill Rescue your own failed attack or ability check with your Bardic die. The original roll stays visible, and the use is spent only if it turns the test into a success.
  • Valor · Combat Inspiration damage Spend your Inspiration while rolling attack damage to include the extra die in the same roll, with critical hits handled for you.
  • Valor · Combat Inspiration defense An incoming hit offers a Reaction to roll the granted Inspiration die for extra AC against that attack. The card updates the outcome and spends the existing grant.

Rest, saves and decisive spells

  • Font of Inspiration. Bardic Inspiration gains native Short Rest recovery while the feature is owned.
  • Countercharm. Eligible friendly failed saves against Charmed or Frightened offer the Bard’s Reaction. Resolve its reroll on the save card with normal Advantage/Disadvantage cancellation.
  • Superior Inspiration. Initiative restores spent Inspiration until two uses are available, respecting the native maximum and preserving a higher balance.
  • Words of Creation. Select one or two targets for eligible Power Word casts. Invalid spacing ends the casting before resources are spent.

Dance

  • Tandem Footwork. Select the checkbox in initiative configuration to spend one Inspiration and share its native die with eligible allies within 30 feet. Rolled allies keep their original dice; allies yet to roll receive the pending bonus.
  • Leading Evasion. The supported Dexterity save benefit extends to qualifying nearby creatures. Other movement and Dance choices remain manual.

Glamour

  • Beguiling Magic. Supported Charm/Fear effects prompt their end-of-turn repeat saves.
  • Mantle of Majesty. Activate through Unearthly Appearance to cast level-1 Command as a free Bonus Action and gain the concentration-linked buff. Later level-1 Commands use the free Bonus Action option; upcasts retain normal slot and action costs. Qualifying targets Charmed by that Bard automatically fail.
  • Unbreakable Majesty. A qualifying hit prompts Recoil; failure stops that attack. The feature tracks its per-turn restriction. Commanded is a reminder until the target’s turn ends; carrying out the command stays manual.

Spirits

  • Gather spirits. Giving Bardic Inspiration offers the native spirit roll. Gathered copies are tracked separately, including duplicates, until used or cleared by rest. Mystical Connection throws both dice together.
  • Spirits from Beyond. Choose Unleash Spirit, Controlled Channeling or Cancel, then confirm the spirit. Controlled Channeling spends its Bonus Action and Inspiration; Unleash uses the chosen gathered copy and the native spirit activity.
  • Empowered Channeling. Add the supported bonus in spell damage/healing configuration. Its Spirit Guardians option grants half cover through that modified casting’s area, including native free casting, while ordinary Spirit Guardians stays separate.

Moon

  • Inspired Eclipse. After giving Inspiration, activate the card control for invisibility and a visible, unoccupied teleport destination within 30 feet. The teleport does not consume movement.
  • Eventide’s Splendor. The Inspiration recipient gets an independent Eclipse option; their teleport uses a Reaction.
  • Lunar Vitality. In eligible healing configuration, choose Yes to spend Inspiration, No for the base healing, or Free with Eventide for 1d6 instead. One selected recipient receives the bonus and +10 Speed until their next turn ends. The shared once-per-turn limit still applies.
  • Blessing of Moonlight. Select it while casting Moonbeam to spend its use and gain the concentration-linked 5-foot dim-light buff. Each failed save against that casting offers its own 2d4 heal for another visible creature within 60 feet. Select the recipient and use the control; initial and later failures are supported, and Lunar Vitality can join the healing roll.

Cleric

Bring supported domain choices into casting, saving throws, damage and healing. Eligible reactions pause application when a decision is needed.

Base class and Light

  • Channel Divinity. Use native Divine Spark and Turn Undead targeting, scaling and costs. Supported Sear Undead damage joins Turn Undead without breaking its own Turned effects.
  • Blessed Strikes. Choose Divine Strike or Potent Spellcasting where applicable. Improved Blessed Strikes can offer its temporary-HP action after qualifying cantrip damage.
  • Warding Flare. React to eligible attacks from their cards, preserving the original roll. Improved Warding Flare offers its native temporary HP before incoming damage continues.
  • Corona of Light. Activate the attached enemy-only area and bright light. Its qualifying saves receive the supported Disadvantage benefit with normal cancellation.

Arcana and Knowledge

  • Modify Magic. Fortifying Spell requires a recorded friendly spell target; Tenacious Spell reduces an eligible successful enemy save. Availability is captured for the casting, with Channel Divinity checked on use.
  • Manifest Magical Knowledge. The Consumption checkbox appears for eligible prepared Divination spells on the Knowledge domain list. Select it to replace spell-slot consumption with Channel Divinity.

Grave

  • Circle of Mortality. Pull of Death adds the native scaling die in damage configuration against wounded creatures. Eligible spell healing against a 0-HP target uses maximum healing dice. Return to Life cantrip handling remains manual.
  • Path to the Grave. Apply the native curse and use its separate rider on a qualifying hit. Choose Radiant or Necrotic in damage configuration; the curse is removed without blocking the main damage workflow.
  • Sentinel at Death’s Door. For an eligible friendly Bloodied attack target within 60 feet, react before damage applies. The reduction halves raw damage before native resistance and rounding.
  • Divine Reaper. Enhanced Necromancy can add a second target to qualifying domain or single-target Necromancy spells. Self-only spells keep native range; material costs per target remain manual. Keeper of Souls stays manually activated with its native charge linked.

Life

  • Blessed Healer. After a qualifying slot-funded spell restores HP to another creature, the Cleric receives the feature’s native self-healing.
  • Disciple of Life and Supreme Healing. The healing roll shows the native slot-based bonus and maximizes eligible healing dice when Supreme Healing applies.
  • Preserve Life. Place the area, then allocate the feature’s healing pool among friendly recipients using the healing sliders.

Trickery and War

  • Invoke Duplicity. Supported illusion positioning supplies attack advantage for the Cleric, expanding to allied attackers with the improved feature. Summoning, movement and Healing Illusion remain native/manual.
  • Guided Strike. An eligible missed self/allied attack offers +10 using Channel Divinity. Assisting another creature uses a Reaction; the original dice remain visible.

Druid

  • Base features: Primal Strike and Potent Spellcasting appear where the Druid rolls damage. Add the extra elemental strike or Wisdom bonus without a second roll, including eligible attacks made in Wild Shape.
  • Wild Shape and Beast Spells: Choose a beast and confirm to transform immediately. With Beast Spells, eligible prepared spells remain on the transformed sheet, while Moon spells keep their own access. Cast and concentrate in beast form, then revert without losing the concentration link. Spells with costly or consumed materials are excluded from Beast Spells access.
  • Moon: Choose Radiant damage for your beast attacks with Lunar Radiance, and reuse that choice on later attacks. Lunar Form offers its extra Radiant damage once per turn. Moonlight Step gives the next attack its Advantage and removes the benefit after use.
  • Land: Choose your land during a Long Rest and let the module prepare its spells and matching resistance. At Short Rest, pick the slots to recover without exceeding Natural Recovery’s budget. Nature’s Sanctuary protects friendly creatures in its area, while Land’s Aid lets you confirm enemies to damage and one ally to heal in the same window.
  • Sea: Manifest the ocean’s protection on yourself or share it through Oceanic Gift. Choose an enemy in each bearer’s reach for the initial burst, resolving the saves with one shared damage roll. On later turns, a Wrath of the Sea action arrives in chat for the bearer’s owner and GM, ready for the next Bonus Action.
  • Stars: Activate Starry Form, pick a constellation and let the module spend Wild Shape and apply the benefits. Archer supplies its first shot immediately and later Bonus Action cards. Healing spells offer a separate Healing Chalice action so you can choose who receives the extra healing. Twinkling offers a start-turn form switch, and Full of Stars comes along when available.
  • Cosmic Omen: Finish a Long Rest to roll your day’s Weal or Woe. When a nearby roll could benefit, the Druid gets an action on that chat card: help an ally succeed or make an enemy fail. The module checks range when the card is created, tracks charges and the Reaction, and updates the roll after use.
  • Summoned areas: Move your Conjure Animals pack and its area follows. Eligible creatures join the turn’s existing save and damage cards instead of starting another damage roll; successful saves take no damage. Once Conjure Elemental restrains a target, repeat saves and damage keep arriving until it breaks free.

Fighter

CorePsi WarriorChampionArcane ArcherBanneret

Battle Masters live for the fight. Choose maneuvers at the point of use in damage Configuration, with attack and damage card actions where needed. No awkward updates or manual dice rerolls—pick your maneuver, take the shot, and keep the fight moving.

The menu shows the maneuvers the Fighter knows and uses their current Superiority Die as they level up. Choose one for the attack, roll its damage with the weapon and let the module keep track of the spent die.

  • Precision Attack A miss offers Precision Attack on the attack card. Add your Superiority Die to that result; if it becomes a hit, continue to damage without rolling the attack again.
  • Trip Attack Choose Trip with your weapon damage. The extra die joins the hit and the target makes its Strength save; failure knocks an eligible creature Prone.
  • Distracting Strike Add your maneuver damage and create an opening for an ally. The next eligible attack receives Advantage, then the opening clears.
  • Menacing Attack Add the maneuver to your hit and prompt the target’s Wisdom save. A failure applies Frightened with the Fighter’s duration tracked for you.
  • Goading Attack Hit, add the maneuver damage and challenge the target. A failed save makes its attacks against other creatures suffer Disadvantage until the effect ends.
  • Maneuvering Attack Add the Superiority Die to damage and leave a visible reminder to choose an ally and resolve their Reaction movement.
  • Pushing Attack Roll the extra damage and Strength save together in the attack flow. On a failed save, the card reminds you to move the target away; token movement stays manual.
  • Relentless Choose whether to spend your usual Superiority Die or use the free Relentless d8. The module tracks that free use each combat turn, including qualifying reactions, and offers it when ordinary dice run out.
  • Cards, effects, and settings Maneuver choices stay visible on their cards, and applied effects can be undone and reapplied. Turn individual automations on or off in the Fighter settings.
  • Parry When a melee hit is about to deal damage, use Parry from its card. Roll the reduction, spend the die and Reaction, and apply the reduced damage.

Great Weapon Fighting and Great Weapon Master are under Feats. Other maneuvers remain manual.

Core Fighter

  • Indomitable. A failed save offers Indomitable right there. Reroll with the Fighter-level bonus and let the card update to the new result.
  • Studied Attacks. Miss a creature and the next attack against it offers Advantage. The module remembers the target and clears the benefit when used or expired.

Psi Warrior

  • Psionic Strike. After a qualifying weapon hit deals damage, click Psionic Strike to roll its extra Force damage. Your Energy Die and once-per-turn use are tracked.
  • Telekinetic Thrust. Using Psionic Strike with Telekinetic Adept? Choose damage alone, Prone or Push in its window. The save follows without another Energy Die; move pushed creatures manually.
  • Protective Field. Protect yourself or a nearby ally from the incoming damage card. Roll an Energy Die and see that creature’s damage reduced before applying it, without reducing damage to anyone else.
  • Native and manual benefits. Keep using Bulwark of Force’s usual controls. Its cover works with supported cover modules without adding the AC bonus twice; situational choices remain at the table.

Champion

  • Survivor · Heroic Rally. A Bloodied Fighter who is still standing receives a healing roll at turn start. The owner can roll it from the prompt, or the table can choose immediate rolls in settings.

Arcane Archer

  • Activate shots manually. Choose and activate your Arcane Shot from its feature card after the attack. Shot selection, Curving Shot and adding the shot’s damage remain manual.
  • Effects finish on time. Banishing, Shadow and Enfeebling effects end when they should, and Enfeebling’s damage reduction uses the originating Fighter’s die.
  • Grasping Shot. A creature caught in the brambles gets a turn-start action reminder for its escape check. A new shot replaces that archer’s previous brambles; movement decisions remain manual.

Banneret

  • Group Recovery and Team Tactics. Activate the feature and pick allies from a list linked to the map. The picker handles range and recipient limits, and Team Tactics applies the group’s temporary Advantage.
  • Shared Resilience. An ally’s failed save offers the Banneret a Reaction. Use Indomitable to reroll it with the Fighter-level bonus, spending the appropriate use and updating the result.
  • Other Fighter features. Continue using the usual feature cards for Tactical Mind, Eldritch Knight choices and other situational actions.

Monk

Core & FlurryOpen HandMercyElementsMystic Arts

Strike hard. Strike fast. Masters of unarmed combat, Monks move quickly and attack just as fast. Choose Stunning Strike and Grapple right in damage Configuration, keeping those decisions together at the actual damage roll so you can keep the fight moving.

  • Stunning Strike Choose Stunning Strike while rolling a qualifying hit’s damage. The module spends Focus, tracks the turn’s use and prompts the target’s Constitution save.
  • Failed and successful saves A failed save applies Stunned. A successful save still applies the feature’s slowed movement and next-attack Advantage, with their durations tracked.
  • Stun before Grapple Choose both on the same hit and Stunning Strike resolves first. If the target is Stunned, its following Grapple save automatically fails.
  • Independent corrections Undo a Stunning Strike or Grapple effect and correct its save without having to undo the weapon’s damage too.

Shared Grapple / Prone prompts are under Common; Grappler’s feat benefits have their own Feats setting.

Initiative, deflection and Focus

  • Uncanny Metabolism. Check it in initiative configuration when available. The completed roll activates its native feature card, restores Focus, spends the Long Rest use, and automatically rolls and applies its native self-healing. Canceling initiative spends nothing.
  • Deflect Attacks / Deflect Energy. An incoming hit offers Deflect on the damage card. Roll to reduce the damage, then follow the eligible redirect option if you reduce it to zero.
  • Disciplined Survivor. A failed save offers the Focus-funded reroll. Use it from the card and keep the replacement result.
  • Flurry of Blows. Follow a two-attack counter for Flurry, increasing to three with Heightened Focus. The module helps keep track of the strikes without extra bookkeeping.

Open Hand

  • Flurry techniques. Choose supported Open Hand techniques alongside your Flurry damage and resolve the save or condition from the same attack flow.

Mercy

  • Hand of Harm. Add Hand of Harm to an eligible hit’s damage and spend Focus there. Supported Physician’s Touch conditions follow the hit.
  • Hand of Healing. Replace a remaining Flurry attack with touch-range healing from the counter, without an additional Focus cost. A canceled healing roll leaves the attack available.
  • Flurry of Healing and Harm. Activate the feature before your first Flurry attack to unlock its extra healing substitutions and free Hand of Harm. The module spends the daily use and keeps the shared Harm limit in view.

Elements

  • Elemental Push / Pull. Choose an elemental push or pull with your damage roll and prompt the required save. Resolve the movement on the map.
  • Elemental Epitome. Choose the supported resistance and let it stay linked to the feature’s active benefits.
  • Destructive Stride. Use Step of the Wind and the feature’s speed boost and damaging aura follow for the turn. Enemies you encounter are collected on one damage card, with each creature hit once and no saving throw.
  • Empowered Strikes. Include the extra damage in the attack’s damage roll, with the once-per-turn use tracked.

Mystic Arts and manual choices

  • Focused Strike. After Stunning Strike resolves, the target has Disadvantage on saves against that Monk’s spells until the Monk’s next turn, whether or not the stun succeeded.
  • Leave movement and casting flexible. Use the normal controls for Mystic Arts spells and make situational movement choices at the table.

Paladin

Holy warriors. Masters of the smite. Focus on landing that critical hit, not juggling extra buttons. Divine Smite and supported prepared Smite spells are built into damage Configuration, so you can choose your smite where the damage happens and bring divine judgment down on your enemies.

  • Divine Smite Choose to smite while rolling weapon damage. Pick the slot, see the extra dice and roll everything together, including the right critical damage.
  • Fiend and Undead bonus Strike a Fiend or Undead and the extra Smite die is included for you.
  • Prepared Smite spells Select an available Smite spell alongside the hit’s damage. Its slot or free use and Bonus Action are spent once, and the follow-up stays linked to that attack.
  • Saves and effects The chosen Smite prompts its required save and applies the appropriate effect. Ongoing damage and repeat saves follow the affected creature, while the damage card shows which Smite was used.

One unified Paladin aura

Move the Paladin and the aura comes with them. Nearby allies receive supported Protection, Courage and oath benefits automatically, then lose them when they leave. Range grows with the character, overlapping Protection auras use the appropriate provider, and an incapacitated Paladin stops granting benefits. The receiving effect shows which Paladin is helping.

Use the actor-window Paladin aura controls to enable a source or choose a preferred Protection provider. Genie Elemental Shielding uses its native feature card: select one resistance, and a later choice replaces the previous one and updates the aura. This choice stays manual, even with automatic effect application enabled.

Disable old Aura Effects Paladin emitters first. Aura outlines show only on the Regions layer. Use Grid Shaped emanations with scene grid spacing and distance matched to the map. Tested with alternating 1–2–1 diagonals; other diagonal rules are unverified.

Supported oath features

  • Noble Genies · Elemental Smite After Divine Smite, choose your elemental follow-up from the damage card. Depending on the element, restrain the target, gain defenses or choose enemies for extra damage or saves. The picker guides the extra targets and the feature use is spent once; forced movement and teleports remain manual.
  • Noble Genies · Elemental Rebuke React to an incoming hit from its card. Choose the element, halve your Paladin’s damage and prompt the attacker’s save and return damage without changing anyone else’s damage.
  • Ancients · Nature’s Wrath Use the initial save and restraint as usual. At the victim’s turn end, the module prompts its escape save and removes that restraint on success.
  • Devotion · Sacred Weapon Activate Sacred Weapon from the attack window. Its attack bonus and light come on together, and the previous lighting returns when the effect ends or the weapon is unequipped.
  • Devotion · Smite of Protection Use Divine Smite and your aura grants its temporary Half Cover to you and nearby allies. Supported cover modules handle it without adding the same AC benefit twice.
  • Devotion · Holy Nimbus Activate Holy Nimbus to light the area, damage nearby enemies at their turn starts and gain supported saving-throw protection. Ending the feature clears its ongoing benefits.
  • Vengeance · Vow of Enmity Choose the marked enemy from the attack window and receive Advantage against it. When that creature falls to 0 HP, transfer the Vow without paying again or resetting its duration.
  • Vengeance · Avenging Angel Activate the form as usual. Enemies starting turns in the aura make their fear saves; failures receive Frightened and supported attacks against them gain Advantage. The fear clears on damage or when its duration ends.

Elder Champion, Noble Scion/Minor Wish, Soul of Vengeance, Relentless Avenger, Inspiring Smite allocation and Living Legend remain table-managed. Keep an active GM connected for managed operations.

Ranger

CoreHunterBeast MasterGloom StalkerFey WandererHollow WardenWinter Walker

Stalk your prey. Know your prey. Hunt your prey. Let the system help track your bonus damage, with Hunter’s Mark and Hunter’s Prey built into damage Configuration. Keep your focus on the hunt while eligible riders join the attack’s damage roll.

  • Hunter’s Prey / Colossus Slayer Add Colossus Slayer while rolling damage against an injured target. The module remembers your choice, includes the right dice and tracks the once-per-turn use.

Hunter’s Mark is grouped with Spells because its rider follows the caster’s concentration and marked target.

Hunter’s Mark and core Ranger features

  • Relentless Hunter. Keep concentrating on Hunter’s Mark without damage-triggered concentration rolls when this feature applies.
  • Precise Hunter and Foe Slayer. Attacks against your marked prey offer Advantage, and Foe Slayer upgrades the Mark’s damage die automatically.

Hunter

  • Choose during a rest. Choose Hunter’s Prey and Defensive Tactics during Short or Long Rest. Your current choices are shown, and the new benefits take effect when the rest finishes.
  • Defensive Tactics. The chosen defense recommends Disadvantage on the qualifying attacks. Escape the Horde follows the documented table interpretation for attacks during the Ranger’s own turn.
  • Superior Hunter’s Defense. React from the incoming damage card and pick the damage type to resist. A breakdown helps with the choice, and only the relevant damage is reduced.
  • Superior Hunter’s Prey. After damaging your marked creature, choose another nearby enemy to receive the same Hunter’s Mark damage. No second damage roll is needed, and the new target’s defenses still apply.

Beast Master

  • Bestial Fury. Your linked Primal Companion adds its supported damage against your marked prey. Keep choosing its commands and attacks as usual.

Gloom Stalker

  • Dreadful Strike. Choose the extra Psychic damage with the weapon roll; the module spends the use and tracks its turn limit.
  • Stalker’s Flurry. After choosing Dreadful Strike, choose Mass Fear for an area save or use Sudden Strike from the damage card. The fear duration is tracked for you.

Fey Wanderer

  • Dreadful Strikes. Extra Psychic damage joins qualifying hits, with each creature tracked separately so you can use it against different enemies in the same turn.
  • Beguiling Twist. Activate the feature, choose Charmed or Frightened, and resolve the save. Repeat saves arrive at turn end and clear the chosen condition on success.
  • Misty Wanderer. Misty Step gains a feature-funded casting option, so the player can spend a Misty Wanderer use instead of a spell slot. Companion placement stays manual.

Hollow Warden

  • Wrath of the Wild. Transform as usual and the fear aura follows your token. Nearby enemies make their saves when the aura is adopted and at your turn start; fear lasts until your next turn.
  • Hungering Might. A qualifying hit while transformed and Bloodied offers your healing roll. The module checks your actual HP and tracks the turn’s use.
  • Rot and Violence. The aura’s failed saves also block healing and Reactions. Strangling Roots lets you choose Sap or Slow alongside the weapon’s other mastery and remembers the choice.
  • Ancient Might. Attack a Frightened creature while transformed and the extra Wisdom damage is included automatically.

Winter Walker

  • Frigid Explorer. Choose Polar Strikes with your weapon damage. The module scales the Cold die and tracks each target, while Biting Cold lets qualifying attacks and spells bypass Cold resistance.
  • Hunter’s Rime. A fresh Hunter’s Mark cast offers your temporary HP roll, including free casts. Moving the existing Mark does not grant it again.
  • Fortifying Soul. Use the healing and hour-long protection as usual. Recognized saves against fear offer Advantage while it lasts.
  • Chilling Retribution. React to an attacker from its damage card and prompt its Wisdom save. On failure it is Stunned with no movement until your next turn ends; the triggering damage still applies.
  • Frozen Haunt. Activate the form while casting Hunter’s Mark and its Cold aura follows you. Nearby enemies receive its damage prompts on activation and your turn start, and the aura clears when the form ends.

Rogue

CoreAssassinSoulknifeThief & Scion

Sneak Attack choices, defensive reactions and subclass follow-ups stay connected to the attack, damage and save cards.

Sneak Attack, Cunning Strike and defense

  • Sneak Attack. Eligible attacks recommend Sneak Attack in the damage window. Confirm it to roll the extra dice with your weapon damage; the module tracks the use, and you can select it yourself when a situational rule applies.
  • Cunning Strike. Trade Sneak Attack dice for Poison, Trip or Withdraw while rolling damage. The window handles the dice cost and later upgrades; supported saves, conditions and repeat saves follow through. Move for Withdraw manually.
  • Devious Strikes. Choose Daze, Obscure or Knock Out with the appropriate Sneak Attack cost. The module prompts saves, tracks durations and handles waking on damage where appropriate.
  • Uncanny Dodge. Use the incoming damage-card action to spend your Reaction and halve your Rogue’s damage before applying it.
  • Evasion. Qualifying Dexterity saves apply no damage on success and half on failure. The save summary identifies Evasion so the GM can see why the damage changed.

Assassin

  • Assassinate. First-round attacks offer the feature’s Advantage against eligible enemies, and qualifying Sneak Attacks include the Surprising Strikes bonus.
  • Envenom Weapons. Failed Cunning Strike Poison saves offer the extra Poison damage, including repeat failures. Poison resistance is bypassed; immunity still protects the target.
  • Death Strike. A qualifying first-round Sneak Attack prompts the extra save before HP is applied. A failure doubles the damage without asking you to roll the original damage again.

Soulknife

  • Homing Strikes. A missed Psychic Blade offers the extra Psionic die on its card. Spend the die only if it turns the miss into a hit, then continue to damage.
  • Rend Mind. Choose Rend Mind after qualifying Psychic Blade Sneak Attack damage. The module uses the available free use or appropriate dice, then handles the Stunned effect and repeat saves.

Thief, Scion and manual subclasses

  • Thief’s Reflexes. The Thief receives a second initiative entry in round one, ten counts lower. It follows the same token and disappears after that extra turn.
  • Scion of the Three · Terrify. Choose Terrify through Cunning Strike, trade the Sneak Attack die and prompt the fear save. Frightened and its repeat saves are handled for you.
  • Leave one-off choices manual. Keep using the normal feature cards for unsupported subclass choices and situational targeting.

Sorcerer

Pure magic, embodied. Control the battlefield, transmute your spells, and overpower your enemies with raw magical force. Let the system handle Metamagic choices during casting and carry them into damage, keeping those decisions connected to the spell instead of managing extra cards afterward.

  • Innate Sorcery: Activate it and your Sorcerer spell attacks offer Advantage while it lasts.
  • Select Metamagic: Choose from one or two compact option dropdowns as permitted by the character’s features. Extra target or element choices appear only for the selected options, with current Sorcery Points and total cost visible before confirmation.
  • Transmuted, Heightened and Careful: Pick an element, give a target Disadvantage on its save, or protect selected allies. Those choices stay connected to the casting and combine with the existing save and damage workflow.
  • Quickened Spell: Cast the eligible spell as a Bonus Action, spend the points and mark the Bonus Action used.
  • Twinned Spell: Keep the original target and add the extra creature on the map. Confirming carries both through the spell’s normal saves and damage without spending a higher-level slot.
  • Subtle, Distant and Extended: Declare them and spend their points in the same window. Their remaining component, range and duration adjustments stay manual.
  • Empowered and Seeking: Reroll selected damage dice or a missed spell attack from the relevant card. The module spends the resource and updates the result while preserving the other dice.
  • Font of Magic: Convert points and slots in one budget-aware picker; available quantities adjust as you choose.
  • Sorcerous Restoration: Choose eligible point recovery in Short Rest.
  • Reaction spells: Shield and other Reaction casts skip the Metamagic confirmation.

Subclass features in play

  • Draconic — Elemental Affinity: Choose the element, gain its resistance and add the matching spell-damage bonus in the roll.
  • Aberrant: Psychic Defenses offers condition-save Advantage. Psionic Sorcery lets eligible spells use Sorcery Points. Revelation in Flesh puts its benefits and total cost in one selection window. Warping Implosion handles its payment choice and caster-centered burst, with a supported teleport afterward.
  • Clockwork: Click Restore Balance on an eligible roll to remove Advantage or Disadvantage using the first original die. Bastion of Law tracks ward dice on its buff and offers a reduction action on incoming damage. Trance of Order applies its supported roll benefits. Clockwork Cavalcade shares its healing pool across the recipients you choose.
  • Shadow: Strength of the Grave offers a recovery action after a recorded damage-card knockout. Beasts of Ill Omen attaches the caster-specific save aura to the native summon. Choose Umbral Form when activating Innate Sorcery if it is available; Shadow Walk stays manual.
  • Spellfire: Choose Crown of Spellfire alongside Innate Sorcery. Burning Life Force offers Hit Point Dice reduction on the damage card, and Spell Avoidance adjusts qualifying save damage.
  • Wild Magic: Use Tides of Chaos in D20 configuration, then resolve its waiting surge from chat. Controlled Chaos shows two results and keeps the one selected. Tamed Surge opens a result picker. Bend Luck adjusts eligible tests from their cards. Surge results offer targeted effects or labeled reminders with Undo; the recurring-surge buff offers a fresh turn-start roll for one minute.

Warlock

  • Pact features: Choose Eldritch Smite or Lifedrinker while rolling a qualifying hit’s damage. The extra dice join the attack, and Lifedrinker can offer Hit Die healing afterward. Familiar owners can choose supported damage types and react to reduce incoming damage through Investment of the Chain Master.
  • Archfey: Choose your Fey Step benefit as you cast Misty Step. Pick affected creatures around your departure or arrival, then resolve the healing, taunts or fear from the linked cards. Short-lived effects clear on time, leaving the player to choose the teleport destination.
  • Celestial: Radiant Soul adds its bonus to qualifying spell damage. At rest, choose allies to receive Celestial Resilience temporary HP. Searing Vengeance guides the selection of a fallen ally, heals them and centers the burst without hand-setting each step.
  • Fiend: Qualifying nearby deaths grant Dark One’s Blessing temporary HP without an unnecessary roll prompt. Use Dark One’s Own Luck from a failed check or save card to add its die. Choose Fiendish Resilience at rest and the selected resistance is applied for you.
  • Great Old One: Pick Psychic damage for eligible spells and reuse your previous choice. Hex and Clairvoyant Combatant keep their target-specific penalties connected. Create Thrall handles the limited-duration summon, and Thought Shield offers reflected damage after Psychic damage is taken.
  • Vestige: Use Semblance of Life to transform your existing Vestige into the stronger spirit form—no spare token or copied actor required. Its scaled attacks and AC are ready, while HP, Hit Dice and Divine Power are retained. Losing the form’s temporary HP or reaching its time limit restores the companion and its features.
  • Undead: Activate Form of Dread and the linked Superior Dread benefits follow. On a qualifying hit, choose Frightful Avatar in the damage window to prompt fear, with the condition ending at the right turn. Grave Touched offers its extra damage and Necrotic choices while handling supported resistance bypass.
  • Reactions: Use supported Warlock reactions, including Beguiling Defenses, from the relevant attack or damage card. The player makes the choice, the module tracks the use and updates the result, and the GM keeps Apply and Undo controls.

0.8.3 feature details →

Wizard

Keep your spellbook’s special castings ready without a second set of counters to manage.

  • Arcane Recovery: Select expended level 1–5 slots during Short Rest. The dropdowns share the Wizard’s recovery budget and narrow as you choose. Completing the rest recovers the selected slots and spends the feature use; canceling or choosing nothing spends nothing.
  • Spell Mastery: Mark spells with the native Mastered enchantment. At base level, Consume Spell Slot starts unchecked. Selecting an upcast level checks it; returning to base level unchecks it. You retain native manual checkbox control.
  • Signature Spells: Use Make Signature to mark the two spells. Each gets one charge, recovered on Short or Long Rest, and a separate Signature Cast/Use activity that casts at base level and spends that charge. The original activity stays ready for normal slot casting and upcasting after the free use is spent.
  • Item enchantments: Choose their inventory recipient through the enchantment card without an unrelated map Retarget button.

v0.8.5 Wizard updates →

Evocation and Abjuration

  • Sculpt Spells. Choose supported friendly protection during area-target confirmation.
  • Potent Cantrip, Empowered Evocation and Overchannel. Supported miss/save damage, the one-roll Intelligence bonus, and optional maximum spell dice appear in the spell workflow. Overchannel tracks its native use and escalating self-damage.
  • Arcane Ward and Projected Ward. Use the native ward tracker and creation reminder, absorb supported incoming damage, or project the benefit to an eligible ally. Undo restores the tracked ward and HP changes.
  • Spell Resistance. Supported spell saves recommend Advantage with normal cancellation; native resistance handles spell damage.

Bladesinger and Conjuration

  • Bladesong and Song of Defense. An active Bladesong buff supplies supported weapon benefits. Song of Defense offers the spell-slot-funded damage reduction from an eligible incoming card.
  • Durable Summons and Focused Conjuration. Supported slot-funded Conjuration summons gain their native benefits; qualifying Conjuration concentration avoids damage-triggered checks.
  • Splintered Summons. Choose the supported extra summon while casting, with native use consumption and concentration cleanup.

Divination, Enchantment and Illusion

  • Portent and Third Eye. Long Rest offers a private Roll Portent reminder. Supported Third Eye benefits clear on Short or Long Rest.
  • Hypnotic Presence and Instinctive Charm. Supported effects retain source-specific range/damage expiry, while eligible incoming hits offer Charm and its save/retarget flow. Qualifying Enchantment casts recharge the feature.
  • Split Enchantment and Illusory Self. Eligible Enchantment spells gain the supported extra target. Illusory Self offers its Reaction on a qualifying attack.

Necromancy and Transmutation

  • Undead Vitality and Grave Power. Use supported Undead healing and Necrotic resistance handling from the feature’s native setup.
  • Extinguish Undead. Eligible defeated Undead offer source-aware actions with the appropriate resource/Reaction cost and native area damage.
  • Transmuter’s Stone. Choose supported benefits after Long Rest and retain one source-tracked stone effect.
  • Empowered Transmutation and Master Transmuter. Choose enhanced native scaling while casting, or use supported Panacea, Restore Life and Restore Youth actions. Major Transformation, age changes and cursed-item decisions remain manual.
